name: aes_sbox
title: The AES S-box (FIPS 197 Section 5.1.1), 8 bits in, 8 bits out

banlist._comment: No operator is banned (decided 10/30): a lookup table, + - * and everything else are legal and simply score what they score. An empty list also switches the Yosys backstop ($alu/$macc/$mul/...) off.

postsynth._comment: The input space is 2^8 = 256 values and the check is made EXHAUSTIVE: the generic fixed vectors (all-0, all-1, walking ones and zeros) are 18 distinct inputs (0, 255, the 8 powers of two and their 8 complements), the task corners are the other 238, so every mode runs all 256 (the light mode keeps at most (light_vectors - 2) / 4 = 249 corners, which holds all 238; the fixed vectors are always kept). tests/aes_sbox/validate/validate.py (step `vectors`) recomputes both unions. `random` is 0 (nothing is left to sample), harvested constants only repeat inputs. ls-sv takes well under a second for the 256 vectors of the 113-gate reference.

references.note: the Boyar-Peralta 113-gate netlist, 113 plain sites: the structure obligations that are quadratic in the sites (one driver per bit, the rank) are decided by the kernel instead of by sv_structure's simp, the rest uses sv_interface and sv_equations; generated by tests/aes_sbox/validate/gen_bp_proof.py, see PROVING.md

the S-box as a 256-entry plain `case` table with a `default` in one always_comb (WP-G S3a), proved by `sv_exhaustive` alone: the design read through its lowering, the `case` compiled once into a word-level table lookup, the 256 inputs decided by kernel evaluation; see PROVING.md, section 15
